# The suite's rules

`mvn test` checks these with every run, whichever tests were asked for: **SuiteRulesTest**, one
entry per rule, reading the sources (no browser, well under a second). It never stops another test:
`mvn test -Dtest=ContactFormTest` runs whatever the rules say. Run them alone: `mvn test -Dgroups=rules`.

Each rule has a **tier**:

- **hard**: the suite's own integrity, and a test that checks nothing. Broken, it fails
  SuiteRulesTest, and so the run.
- **story**: how a story is written. It holds for stories only (a test carrying `@Story` or
  extending `StoryTest`) and fails SuiteRulesTest like a hard rule. A test of your own that is not a
  story is held to the hard rules only.
- **advisory**: the suite's conventions. Broken, it is a warning in the run's output and in
  `target/rules-report.md`, whose first line counts the warnings (for CI to gate on, if a team wants).

| Rule | Tier | What must be true | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SR-01 | story | A story is in cases/ | One folder holds every story, generated tests beside them. |
| SR-02 | story | A story stands on StoryTest | StoryTest is BaseTest (a test's browser, its numbered plain-English step log, the evidence of a failure: screenshot, the page's HTML, a trace) with the story's id in the log. |
| SR-03 | story | A story names its story | The id ties the test to the story in the team's tracker and in stories/done/: the run log prints it, a failure points back to it, and SR-17 and SR-18 check the two stay together. |
| SR-04 | story | A story class is named after its id | Anyone holding a story id finds its test by name, in cases/, without searching: that is what makes a stale story easy to delete. |
| SR-05 | story | Each story id is used once | One story, or one requirement of it, one test: a second class with the same id is a copy that drifts from the first, and deleting "the" test of a stale story leaves the other behind. |
| SR-06 | advisory | A story is one test | A story is one visitor's journey with one outcome. |
| SR-07 | advisory | A story has one check | "One verify per story" (Ghost, 2026-09-28): a story states one outcome, and its test proves that one. |
| SR-08 | advisory | The check comes last | The check is the story's outcome, so the story ends there. |
| SR-09 | advisory | A story's test reads as its title | The report and the run log show the display name: with the story's title there, a person who never opens the code reads which story passed or failed. |
| SR-10 | story | A story uses page objects, not Playwright | A story reads like the story because every step is a page method named for what a visitor does ("click().learnMore()"). |
| SR-11 | advisory | A story does not assert | Checks live in the pages' verify() methods, built on Checks, which log the step and fail in plain English ("Expected the email input to hold ..."). |
| SR-12 | advisory | Nothing sleeps | A sleep is too long on a fast day and too short on a slow one: the test gets slower and still flaky. |
| SR-13 | advisory | No regular expressions in tests and pages | Tests and pages are read and changed by people who aren't programmers; a regular expression is where they stop understanding. |
| SR-14 | advisory | A test switched off says why | A test switched off without a word hides a failure and is forgotten; with its reason, the next person knows whether it can come back. |
| SR-15 | hard | YOURS blocks keep both marker lines | Regenerating keeps what is between a block's two marker lines, and only that. |
| SR-16 | hard | Generated files change only inside YOURS blocks | Regenerating the suite (a new crawl of a changed site) rewrites everything outside YOURS blocks, so a change made there silently disappears. |
| SR-17 | story | Every story in stories/done/ has its test | stories/done/ is the record of which stories the suite checks. |
| SR-18 | story | Every story test has its story in stories/done/ | The story file is the test's reason to exist, in the words of whoever asked for it; without it nobody can tell whether the test still checks something wanted. |
| SR-19 | hard | Every test checks something | A test that only acts (opens a page, clicks a link) and checks nothing passes whenever nothing throws: it can't tell the right page from the wrong one, and a green run says less than it seems. |
| SR-20 | hard | Account files stay out of git | An account in git is an account everyone with the repository has, and every copy of it handed on; a suite travels to dev teams, pipelines and tracker apps. |
| SR-21 | story | A done story's notes name every criterion, by its number | A criterion's number is its test's name (&lt;id>-&lt;n>): a list edited after its tests were written moves every number after the edit, so a test checks one criterion under another's number, and a criterion left out of the notes is a part of the story nobody checks, or says is unchecked (trial 7: 3 of 3 list edits renumbered tested stories). |
| SR-22 | hard | One element, one name | Every test then reaches one element two ways, and a locator fixed under one name is still broken under the other; two stories written apart (two branches) each add their own name for the same button and merge without a conflict. |

Every rule in full (what it checks, exactly, how to fix a failure, a wrong and a right example):
[ai/rules-in-full.md](ai/rules-in-full.md).

The rules files (SuiteRules.java, SuiteRulesTest.java, this file and `src/test/resources/suite-rules/fingerprints.txt`) are generated
with the suite. A change to one is a change outside a YOURS block: regenerating overwrites it, SR-16
reports it, and `suite verify playwright-playground-com-tests` finds it by comparing every generated file with what
Suite Builder generates. To change a rule, change Suite Builder.
